title: Two Unprecedented 3-Connected Three-Dimensional Ne
one_line_summary: Design rule: use ligands with specific geometry to direct rigid square-planar secondary building units

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: copper-mediated cycloaddition forming copper(I) triazolate coordination polymer → stability

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: large 3D channels interpenetrated by an identical translational net → porosity

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] use ligands with specific geometry to direct rigid square-planar secondary building units → has successfully produced targeted network structures

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] control the dihedral angles between adjacent square-planar nodes → enables assembly of specific 3D network topologies instead of the commonly favored 2D 4^4 grids

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: Cu(OH)2 replacement condition in another synthesis vs Cu2(OH)2CO3-based original condition in the same synthesis: winner=subject_b on product_yield

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: ligands with methyl substituents in compound 1 vs ligands with larger propyl substituents in compound 2: winner=subject_b on adjacent-node_dihedral_angle

key_insights.title: Failure
key_insights.body: [performance_regression] assemble extended structures solely from square-planar building blocks without controlling adjacent-node orientation: formation of 3D networks is disfavored because 2D square-grid 4^4 nets are favored

notable_quotes: Crystallography shows each triazolate is μ3-tridentate and each Cu(I) is trigonal-planar, producing novel 3D 3-connected nets in both 1 and 2.
The copper-mediated hydrothermal reaction of nitriles and ammonia is presented as a novel non-hydrazine route to 3,5-disubstituted 1,2,4-triazoles.
Topology in square-planar-node networks depends strongly on adjacent-node dihedral angles; methyl vs propyl substituents (~30° vs ~90°) likely enforce them sterically.
